seed_context.note: Determinism is controlled entirely via ElkanotoPuClassifier(random_state=...) and LogisticRegression(random_state=...); lbfgs is itself a deterministic solver given fixed data, so no separate global numpy/torch seed call is needed or made by this module.

training.base_estimator_decision: Base estimator: sklearn.linear_model.LogisticRegression(max_iter=2000, random_state=<config.train_seed>), default L2 penalty, C=1.0 (sklearn's own default). No pre-specified base-classifier/architecture for Two-Step PU or PU-Bagging was found in docs/PU_AOP_RESEARCH_CONTEXT.md, the Planner doc, or the proposal (inspected directly before writing this module, not assumed). Logistic regression was chosen over a tree ensemble (e.g. RandomForestClassifier) because it is the more common choice in the original Two-Step PU (Elkan & Noto 2008) and PU-Bagging (Mordelet & Vert 2014) literature, is simpler to reason about and faster to fit/reproduce exactly, and keeps both new baselines on the SAME base-estimator family for a cleaner later comparison between them. Wrapping the existing torch BinaryMlp as a scikit-learn estimator merely to force architectural uniformity with PN/nnPU was explicitly considered and rejected as a disproportionate engineering detour for a baseline-implementation task -- see docs/IMPLEMENTATION_STATUS.md's Task 4.4 decision log entry.
training.label_encoding_note: y=1 encodes an E1/E2 labeled positive; y=0 encodes a C1 row passed to the scikit-learn/pulearn estimator's unlabeled-surrogate slot. This 0 is a library-API numeric requirement (pulearn's PU estimators accept exactly one 'unlabeled' numeric code and have no three-way positive/unlabeled/negative label type), not a project-level claim that C1 is a confirmed negative -- see AGENTS.md rule #1 and this module's own docstring.
training.no_learning_curve_reason: Two-Step PU's .fit() is a single, non-iterative procedure (one hold-out split, one classifier fit, one scalar correction constant) -- there is no per-epoch optimization trajectory to plot, unlike PN/nnPU's mini-batch training loops.
